judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: The urgent 'Damn! Where have you been, lad!?' fits Jandor, but 'leaving rebuilding the village our smallest concern' is a strained construction, and the set-up packs a whole battle summary into the opening.

items.label: B
items.critique: The stiff self-introduction in fragments ('The Master for the [Place].'), the shouted 'YOU carry the staff' and the plain 'Speak to one of the Priests' journal are Westwood's late-campaign stiffness.

items.label: C
items.critique: 'Too many prying eyes the closer we get by air' is awkward, and 'Forest beasts will heed its bite should they threaten' is a literary flourish Jandor doesn't use. It reads as a drop-off scene modelled on Westwood's.

items.label: D
items.critique: 'Sorry about the stench, lad', the frank 'This may get very ugly', and a reminder that just explains what the given spells are for read like Westwood's practical briefing voice.

items.label: E
items.critique: 'No time to rest on laurels', 'the unlucky [Place]' and a speech that names three masked people in a row feel assembled. The reminder repeats the opening's last line, which is plausible, but the whole is generic.

items.label: F
items.critique: The mentor's formal, slightly ungrammatical exposition ('Wildlife incursions ... is on a steady rise'), 'scry', 'antiquated records' and a reminder naming 'book and amulet' are authentic Westwood quest-giver prose.

items.label: G
items.critique: The clipped 'You'll know. And careful.' is good, but the reminder restates the opening almost word for word with an extra 'Hurry!', a seam that could be either side. It is a toss-up.

items.label: H
items.critique: The drop-off formula ('This is as far as I can safely take you', 'You remain our only hope', 'chit-chat') is very Jandor, possibly too close to a template. The journal line is plain and good.

items.label: I
items.critique: The over-hearty welcome, 'gone mad!', the capital-E 'East of here', 'nettlesome urchins' and a reminder that is just a grumble rather than an instruction are characteristic Westwood.

items.label: J
items.critique: The exclamatory tour-guide arrival with double dashes and the curt 'It weeds out the weak recruits' are classic Westwood arrival lines.

tells: Westwood's reminders often add nothing new (a grumble, 'press on now, lad') or simply repeat the order. The new ones are more crafted.
Literary flourishes (a staff whose 'bite' beasts will heed, 'rest on laurels', 'unlucky [Place]') mark the new writing; Westwood's mentor-speak is formal but literal and sometimes ungrammatical.
New openings compress a whole backstory, with cause, consequence and stakes, into one speech; Westwood's openings give a place, a person and an order.
The guide's voice was hard to separate in this packet, since both sides use 'lad', exclamations and drop-off formulas. Confidence is low on the boundary items.
